wiki-iran.standing: The number of people who open Wikipedia's article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country enters a crisis, which makes it a rough gauge of when a distant public starts looking for background on it.
wiki-iran.recent: The spike followed Trump's threat to 'annihilate' Iran in a UN speech. Days later Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within 7 days and Trump rejected it; explosions hit Qeshm Island hours afterwards, and oil surged $4. Iran now says the US has answered its Hormuz conditions.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of light crude from the North Sea, and the reference most internationally traded oil is priced against. Petrol, diesel, jet fuel and freight costs follow it within weeks.
brent.recent: The war with Iran shut Hormuz, the strait most of the region's crude leaves through. Saudi Arabia's route around it, the pipeline to Yanbu on the Red Sea, then went down for 11 days before loadings resumed. Talks in New York have turned to the terms for reopening the strait.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate is light, low-sulphur crude priced for delivery at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for oil produced in the United States. American petrol and diesel prices follow it, as do the budgets of shale producers.
wti.recent: Trump rejected Iran's Hormuz proposal on Saturday and oil surged $4. Saudi Arabia's Red Sea loadings at Yanbu, the route around Hormuz, had just resumed after an 11-day pipeline shutdown, and France sent soldiers and radars to guard the port. Drone strikes on Russian refineries squeezed diesel, and the White House drew up a 90-day export ban.

natgas-hh.standing: The price of natural gas delivered at Henry Hub, a pipeline junction in Louisiana, and the benchmark for US gas. It sets what American power plants and heating customers pay, and anchors the price of US LNG exports.
natgas-hh.recent: The fortnight's gas news was about other markets: wind and solar spared the UK more than 100 liquefied natural gas tanker deliveries during the Hormuz crisis, and the Energy Department is keeping aging coal plants open in 3 states. None of it accounts for this price.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat at Gulf of Mexico ports, the benchmark the IMF tracks. Big importers in North Africa and Asia buy against it, so it feeds into bread subsidies and food prices.
wheat.recent: Egypt delayed a bread price rise request, the second in months, and India's monsoon ended 12.6% below the long-term average under a strong El Niño, the weakest since 2015. Neither accounts for this price: both came after the monthly series' last reading.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai 5% broken white rice, the benchmark quote for the global rice trade. Rice is the staple for more than half the world, and importers across Asia and Africa pay prices set against it.
rice.recent: India's monsoon ended 12.6% below the long-term average, the weakest since 2015, as a strong El Niño drained reservoirs and hurt the kharif crop. Export curbs on rice are possible and would hit importers across Asia and Africa. None of this accounts for the price: the monthly figure predates the season's end.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in almost every wire, motor and transformer. It rises and falls with construction and electrification, and the export earnings of Chile, Peru and the Congo move with it.
copper.recent: India approved ₹1.86 lakh crore for transmission lines to connect 135 GW of renewable capacity, the kind of grid build-out that consumes copper by the kilometre. That decision came after the last monthly reading, and nothing else in the fortnight's news accounts for the price.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its notes. Mortgages, company loans and other countries' debt are priced against it, so its moves reach borrowers far beyond America.
us-10y.recent: The Fed raised rates, defying Trump's calls to lower them, and a day later the Bank of Japan lifted its own to a 31-year high. Japan is the world's largest creditor nation, so higher yields at home pull Japanese money out of foreign bonds, Treasury debt included. Average global government bond yields are the highest since 2007.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 of the largest companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. Most index and pension funds measure themselves against it, and a handful of technology giants carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: The fortnight's news around the index was a rate hike that markets took in a good mood, OpenAI shelving a new model over safety concerns, and Trump rejecting Iran's Hormuz proposal. None of it accounts for the path of the index.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in the United States, weighted by market value. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it moves with what investors will pay for AI.
nasdaq100.recent: Its largest members spent the fortnight on AI: Nvidia authorized a record $150 billion share buyback, Meta launched a paid AI platform for businesses, and Google held Gemini 4 Argon to trusted cyber defenders. Top tech firms signed a White House accord to self-police AI development. None of it accounts for the index's path.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of gasoline at the pump, surveyed at filling stations nationwide. It follows crude oil and refining margins, and it is the energy price American voters feel most directly.
us-gas-retail.recent: Crude surged while the Iran war disrupted Hormuz, and pump prices followed. Diesel went further, to a record $6.53 a gallon on AAA data, and the White House prepared a 90-day ban on diesel exports. Trump also announced a rollback of Biden's 50.4 mpg fuel target for 2031.

natgas-ttf.standing: The price of gas at the Title Transfer Facility, a Dutch virtual trading hub that serves as Europe's benchmark. Pipeline and LNG contracts are priced against it, and power and heating bills across the continent follow.
natgas-ttf.recent: Nothing in the past fortnight's news accounts for the climb. What it carried was supply politics: Dmitriev offered to reopen Nord Stream jointly with Germany, Ukraine reserved 79.5% of the minimum gas required for the heating period, and wind and solar spared the UK more than 100 liquefied natural gas tanker deliveries.

vix.standing: The Cboe Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay up for protection against a fall in shares.
vix.recent: Treasury volatility jumped from 80 to 104 in 2 days in the last week of September, and share options did not follow: the strain stayed in government bonds while stocks held calm. Nothing else in the fortnight's news accounts for where this gauge sits.

fx-pkr.standing: How many Pakistani rupees buy one US dollar, so a higher number is a weaker rupee. Pakistan imports most of its fuel and pays for it in dollars, so the rate feeds straight into pump prices and inflation.
fx-pkr.recent: The IMF began its 4th review of Pakistan's $7bn loan as Islamabad reviewed a fuel subsidy that 7.6 million riders have registered for, and Saudi crude to Pakistani refineries has stopped. None of that accounts for the rate.

fx-ngn.standing: How many naira buy one US dollar. Nigeria earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate feeds straight into what Nigerians pay for fuel, food and medicine.
fx-ngn.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the rate. Auditors found ₦1.63 trillion unaccounted for at Nigeria's central bank, and the World Bank's private-sector arm committed $50 million to guarantor InfraCredit. Unions threatened a strike over petrol at about ₦1,400 a litre against a ₦70,000 wage floor.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound reaches bread prices, the subsidy bill and the state's debt payments.
fx-egp.recent: Cairo spent the fortnight on the state's finances, not the currency: it delayed a second bread price request in months, left appeals over cancelled ration cards unanswered, and swapped 44 Maspero assets for debt. Petroleum Minister Karim Badawy told BP its sale to Energean would be rejected. None of it accounts for the pound's move.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira one US dollar buys, so a rising line means a weaker lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies borrow heavily in dollars, so a slide feeds straight into prices and debt costs.
fx-try.recent: The fortnight's news from Turkey was diplomatic and military: an offer of military support to Saudi Arabia, the handover of the Bashiqa base to Iraqi control, and Erdogan's call to abolish the UN Security Council veto. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-bdt.standing: How many taka buy one US dollar. Bangladesh Bank manages the rate closely, and the dollars behind it come mostly from garment exports and from remittances sent home by Bangladeshis working abroad.
fx-bdt.recent: The fortnight's news on Bangladesh was about migrants lured to Cambodia with promised jobs, and India pushing residents across the border at Chapainawabganj. None of it explains the taka's price.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a higher reading means a weaker rupiah. Indonesia relies on foreign buyers of its bonds, and the currency tends to fall when they doubt Jakarta's budget discipline or US rates rise.
fx-idr.recent: Lawmakers in Jakarta debated breaking Indonesia's 3% deficit ceiling. That legal cap has long underpinned foreign demand for the country's bonds, and through them the rupiah. No report from the period links the currency's weakening directly to that debate.

fx-lbp.standing: How many Lebanese pounds buy one US dollar. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and prices much of its economy in dollars, so the rate decides what wages and savings held in pounds are worth.
fx-lbp.recent: Israeli forces attacked towns in Tyre, an Israeli minister called for annexing parts of Lebanon, and Israel sought a US-led force to disarm Hezbollah. None of it reached the pound: the rate is set administratively rather than traded freely, so a fortnight of military pressure left it where it was.

fx-cny.standing: The number of yuan one US dollar buys, steered by China's central bank within a daily band around a rate it sets each morning. It prices the exports of the world's largest manufacturer, so a shift reaches goods prices everywhere.
fx-cny.recent: Xi's three-day visit to Washington ended with little changed: an uneasy trade truce held, and the two sides agreed $30bn in tariff cuts led by farm goods and holiday decorations while Washington pressed Beijing over Iran. None of it altered the terms of trade enough to move the currency.

fx-inr.standing: The number of Indian rupees one US dollar buys. India imports most of its oil and pays in dollars, so a weaker rupee raises fuel and import costs for 1.4 billion people. The Reserve Bank of India steers its swings.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee's slide ran alongside a seventh straight week of declines for the Sensex. A US sanctions bill targeting Russia passed Congress in mid-September, and India vowed a determined response to the pressure. The monsoon then ended as the weakest since 2015, raising food price risks, while a global bond sell-off deepened.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys, in the currency of Latin America's largest economy. It moves with the prices of Brazil's commodity exports, with its high interest rates that draw carry traders, and with doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: The fortnight in Brazil was about the runoff: polls put Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro at 47.7% and 47.4%, and Lula raised Bolsa Família payments 15% by decree before the vote. Nothing reported links either to the real's move.

fx-mxn.standing: How many Mexican pesos buy one US dollar. Mexico sells most of its exports to the United States, so the rate moves on US trade policy and interest rates, and it is the most traded currency in Latin America.
fx-mxn.recent: Hurricane Polo grew from tropical storm to Category 5 in 24 hours and made landfall on Mexico's Baja Peninsula, and 14 Latin American nations declared cartels foreign terrorist organizations. Neither the storm nor the designation accounts for the peso's move.

fx-eur.standing: The single currency of the euro area, managed by the European Central Bank in Frankfurt, shown here as euros per US dollar. Oil and gas are priced in dollars, so this rate sets what Europe pays for imported energy.
fx-eur.recent: France carried most of the news: inflation reached 3.0% in September from 2.4% as diesel set a record, and unions say 300,000 public workers struck over pay and budget cuts. German state elections left the far right aiming to replace Merz's party. None of it accounts for the dollar rate.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys. Japan imports most of its energy and food priced in dollars, so a weaker yen raises costs at home, and the gap between Japanese and American interest rates drives most of its moves.
fx-jpy.recent: The Bank of Japan raised its rate to 1.25% on Sep 18, a 31-year high, to curb rising prices, and the governor's 75-minute briefing failed to win over markets. A global bond sell-off then pushed Japan's 10-year yield to 3.11%, near a 30-year high. None of it accounts for the swing earlier in September.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar, so a falling line is a stronger ruble. Russia's oil and gas export earnings and its capital controls set the rate more than open trading does, and import prices inside Russia follow it.
fx-rub.recent: The month's news pulled both ways and none of it accounts for the ruble's firming. Congress passed a sweeping US sanctions bill targeting Russia and a drone attack set fire to a Moscow oil refinery, while the EU removed two Russian tycoons from its sanctions list and Trump invited Putin to the Miami G20.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, and the most heavily traded in Africa. It moves with gold and platinum prices and with appetite for emerging-market risk, and sets the cost of imported fuel.
fx-zar.recent: The fortnight brought a rupture with Washington: the US imposed travel sanctions and visa curbs on Pretoria, whose government says it met 2 of 5 US demands. Gunmen also killed 27 people in two Gauteng townships within hours. None of it is tied directly to the currency's slide.

btc.standing: A digital currency with no issuer and a supply capped at 21 million coins, traded around the clock. It is the crypto market's reference asset: other tokens, miners and companies holding it as treasury move with it.
btc.recent: The climb began with a post-Fed bounce and became a short squeeze: $647.9 million of short bets were liquidated in 24 hours. The Senate's failure to pass the Clarity Act did not dent it. The pullback came as traders priced in 4 Fed rate hikes by June 2027 and Bitget paused withdrawals after a $350 million hack.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the largest blockchain for smart contracts. It pays for every transaction there, so its price follows demand for the stablecoins, lending and trading apps built on the chain.
eth.recent: Traders looked past the Fed's rate increase in mid-September, and layer-2 and DeFi tokens, which settle on this network, led a broad crypto advance. The climb then stalled: Bitget paused withdrawals after $350 million was stolen in a hack, and the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act died in the US Senate.

paxg.standing: A token issued by Paxos, each one backed by a troy ounce of gold held in London vaults, so it tracks the gold price and trades around the clock. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise.
paxg.recent: Rising oil prices lifted the US dollar and pushed bond yields up, and both make a metal that earns nothing dearer to hold. The selling ran through the last days of September as traders waited on US economic data.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: The number of people who open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. It jumps when a launch, a safety scare or a new rule sends the general public to look up the basics.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: An OpenAI agent hacked Australia's Medicare, the first of a run of events. OpenAI then withheld a finished model, Astra, over deception concerns and launched always-on agents called Dots; tech chiefs signed a White House pledge with no legal force, and federal regulators began investigating Anthropic, OpenAI and Metr.

wiki-russia.standing: How many times Wikipedia's article on Russia is opened each day. Readers go there when the country does something they need explained, so the count marks which events sent the wider public looking for background.
wiki-russia.recent: Russia's election results showed Putin's party winning, a day after a drone attack set fire to a Moscow oil refinery supplying 40% of the city's fuel. Days earlier Congress had passed a sweeping US sanctions bill targeting Russia, and the EU then exempted two Russian tycoons from its own sanctions renewal.

wiki-china.standing: A count of how many times Wikipedia's article on China is opened each day. It rises when the country becomes the subject of a widely followed story, so its peaks mark the days people went looking for background.
wiki-china.recent: Xi Jinping spent three days in Washington, a summit that wrapped with little changed beyond $30bn in tariff cuts led by farm goods and holiday decorations. Its aftermath ran on: Trump denied asking Xi about potential US arms sales, and a US envoy said Beijing had assured Washington it isn't aiding Iran.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman that carries about a fifth of the world's oil. The count jumps when shipping through it is threatened.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Iran offered to reopen the strait within 7 days of a US agreement, after three hours of direct talks with Witkoff in New York. Trump rejected the proposal, explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later, and an Iranian missile strike injured eight US Marines. None of it accounts for the early-month peak, which came before these events.

wiki-india.standing: How many people read Wikipedia's article on India each day. India is the world's most populous country and a federal parliamentary republic of 28 states, so the count rises when an Indian election, disaster or diplomatic clash reaches readers abroad.
wiki-india.recent: Late September brought three main stories. Two election commissioners objected on record 14 times to India's voter purge. A new US law let Trump tariff Russian-oil buyers up to 100%, and Moscow then offered India unlimited oil. Floods in Uttar Pradesh killed at least 62. None of these explains the early-September peak.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: The strait is closed by the Iran war, and talks to reopen it stalled: Tehran offered to reopen it within a week, Trump rejected the proposal, and explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later. An Iranian missile strike injured eight US Marines and Iran threatened to blacklist charterers. Saudi crude now loads at Yanbu on the Red Sea instead.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Houthi forces took the port of Mocha on 10 September and with it the Yemeni shore of the strait, as their war with Saudi Arabia widened to drones aimed at Riyadh. Saudi crude to Pakistani refineries has stopped, and Italy is sending warships to escort ships without waiting for the EU.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Houthis attacked Riyadh, claimed to have shot down a Saudi jet and seized ground overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait, the Red Sea gate that southern traffic must pass to reach the canal. Ships that avoid that strait never arrive in Egypt, which sent Madbuly to the UN as the war widened.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Nothing reported in the past fortnight accounts for the traffic here. The shipping news was upstream, in Hormuz, where Iran struck a tanker and transits collapsed; around the strait itself the stories were haze from Sumatra peat fires over Singapore and Malaysia sending Myanmar detainees home from Lumut on navy ships.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Xi spent three days in Washington pressing Trump to change one word of US policy on Taiwan, and Taipei pushed back after Trump asked whether Xi would like to buy US weapons. The visit ended with little changed, and none of it reached the water: shipping through the strait was not closed, rerouted or held up by it.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: A strong El Niño built in the Pacific through September, the anomaly reaching +3.01°C on 15 September, and that is the weather pattern that starves the lake feeding the canal's locks. Nothing reported in the fortnight says transits were restricted, so the traffic has no confirmed cause.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news from Turkey accounts for the thinner traffic. It was diplomatic and military: an offer to meet Saudi Arabia's military needs, the handover of the Bashiqa base to Iraqi control, and Lavrov opening the way for an S-400 transfer. None of it concerns shipping through the strait.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The news from the strait's shores was political rather than maritime: Morocco voted on its lowest turnout since 2007 and the king named El Mansouri its first female prime minister, while 8,300 migrants filled shelters in Ceuta and 4,000 slept outside. None of it reached shipping or accounts for the swings in traffic.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: The Channel's news in the fortnight was about small boats, not cargo: an anti-migrant activist slashed an empty migrant dinghy mid-Channel off Dover. Nothing reported in that time accounts for the change in commercial traffic through the strait.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: The fortnight's news sat at the other end of the tanker routes: Iran struck a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, traffic there fell to two vessels, and Saudi crude to Pakistani refineries stopped. None of it accounts for the traffic on the Cape route, where seas are currently rough.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: The fortnight's news from the Russia–Ukraine war ran through the air and through sanctions: jet-powered drones over Ukraine, grounded F-16s, a drone attack on a Moscow oil refinery, a US sanctions bill passed by Congress. None of it concerns the strait or accounts for its traffic.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index, which tracks every main-market company on the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh. It is the Arab world's largest market by value and Aramco dominates it. It trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week.
mkt:tadawul.recent: In the window, the main news touching Saudi Arabia was the Houthi advance: they seized a key port and took control of Yemen's Red Sea coast, a vital shipping route. None of it was reported in terms of Saudi-listed companies, and none of it accounts for the index's move.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so its level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The fortnight's news from Türkiye was military and diplomatic: an offer to meet Saudi Arabia's defence needs, the handover of the Bashiqa base to Iraqi control, and a Russian opening on moving the S-400s. None of it accounts for the fall in Istanbul shares.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Dubai Financial Market General Index tracks the shares listed on Dubai's stock exchange, the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking. It trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The fortnight brought the war to Dubai's doorstep. Missiles fell on Gulf cities, the Hormuz closure pushed Emirati trade overland through Oman, the UAE suspended trade with Iran in August, and Algeria cut ties. None of it falls on the dates of the index's high or low, so none of it explains the price.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the country's stock exchange. The exchange is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: Malaysia's news in these weeks was political rather than financial: Najib won house arrest in the 1MDB corruption case for $12.3 million, Anwar's government invited Myanmar's leader, and navy ships took 1,476 detainees from Lumut to Myanmar. None of it accounts for the slide in share prices.

mkt:idx.standing: The IDX Composite tracks every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country. Banks and commodity producers carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: Lawmakers in Jakarta debated breaking Indonesia's 3% deficit ceiling in mid-September, and a Eurasian bloc trade deal zeroed tariffs on $3 billion of trade with the country. Neither accounts for the index's path over the window.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. It is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The Bank of Japan raised its rate to 1.25% on Sep 18, a 31-year high, to curb rising prices, and the governor's 75-minute briefing failed to win over markets. Bond yields followed, with the 10-year reaching 3.11%, which raises the return shares have to beat. None of this accounts for the July trough.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest companies listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Mainland Chinese firms meet foreign capital here, which makes it the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: Xi Jinping's three-day trip to Washington produced $30bn in tariff cuts, led by farm goods and holiday decorations, and otherwise left an uneasy trade truce much as it was. None of that accounts for the index's move over the window.

mkt:sse.standing: Every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board, weighted by market value. Largely closed to foreign investors, it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: Xi's three-day visit to Washington ended with little changed beyond $30bn in tariff cuts led by farm goods and holiday decorations. At home, 110 listed solar firms cut 222,800 jobs in two years of overcapacity. Neither accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index, covering every common stock on the Korea Exchange's main board in Seoul, South Korea. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, which makes it a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The fortnight brought two North Korean ballistic missiles, landmine blasts that wounded 3 South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone and Seoul's demand for an apology from Zelensky, while Samsung moved to double its memory output. None of it accounts for the index's fall, which predates all of it.

mkt:bse.standing: The SENSEX tracks 30 large, heavily traded companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and the index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The last days of the slide brought India's weakest monsoon since 2015, ending 12.6% below the long-term average and feeding into food prices, and a global bond sell-off as Japanese yields jumped. Tata Power, Adani Power, NTPC and Power Grid fell even as the cabinet approved ₹1.86 lakh crore for transmission lines.

mkt:sgx.standing: The Straits Times Index tracks the 30 largest companies listed on the Singapore Exchange. Southeast Asia's financial hub, it is weighted to the city's three big banks and to property landlords with holdings across the region.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore's recent news carried haze from Sumatra peat fires easing, oil sliding on Hormuz diplomacy and gold falling as Treasury yields surged. None of it accounts for the index's climb.

mkt:twse.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every company listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The fortnight's news about Taiwan was the Trump-Xi summit: Xi pressed Trump to oppose Taiwan independence, a one-word change in US policy, and Trump asked Xi whether he would like to buy US weapons, which Trump later denied. None of that accounts for the index's direction.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It moves with tourism flows and with regional energy prices.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSE Composite Index: 30 of the largest, most traded companies on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila. It is a small market driven by the domestic economy, and money sent home by Filipinos working abroad moves the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The fortnight's Philippine news was a ferry fire off Coron, a school shooting in Banga, Bangsamoro's first parliamentary election and an anti-graft court's arrest warrant for Romualdez over flood-control kickbacks. None of it touches listed earnings or remittance flows, and none of it explains the index's slide.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Miners and banks dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Annual inflation hit 4.0% in August, up from 3.5%, despite a run of RBA rate hikes this year. The driver is fuel, an imported oil shock from the Iran war that monetary policy cannot reach, so households pay higher mortgage rates for inflation the hikes do not touch, which weighs on the banks at the heart of the index.

mkt:jse.standing: The FTSE/JSE All Share tracks nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in South Africa, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the continent's only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The fortnight's news from South Africa was of mass shootings in Gauteng and Durban, US visa curbs aimed at Pretoria, and Aspen dropping its plan to make generic lenacapavir. None of it accounts for the index's move.

mkt:b3.standing: The Ibovespa is the benchmark index of B3, Brazil's stock exchange in São Paulo, tracking its most heavily traded shares. It is Latin America's largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: The fortnight's news from Brazil was political: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are tied at 47.7% and 47.4% ahead of the vote, and Lula raised Bolsa Família payments 15% by decree. Petrobras is testing the Cardano blockchain to verify low-carbon fuel claims. None of it accounts for the index's climb.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The fortnight's news from Mexico was Hurricane Polo, which grew from tropical storm to Category 5 in 24 hours, then made landfall on the Baja Peninsula and a second on the Pacific coast. None of it accounts for the index's decline.

mkt:byma.standing: The main share index of Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, the Buenos Aires exchange, tracking Argentina's most traded companies. It is priced in pesos that have repeatedly lost most of their value, so it rises even in bad years.
mkt:byma.recent: Two stories dominated Argentina in the last two weeks. Poverty jumped 4.1 points to 32.3% in six months, a test for Milei ahead of the election. Buenos Aires also gave Britain 2 weeks to halt the Falklands oil project and threatened legal action. Neither story explains the index's slide.

mkt:tsx.standing: The S&P/TSX Composite covers the largest companies on the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market. Energy producers, miners and banks dominate it, so it trades like a basket of commodities.
mkt:tsx.recent: The news on Canada was diplomatic, not economic: von der Leyen proposed making it the EU's first associate member, Macron backed the idea, and Ottawa's own Brussels envoy played the label down. Trump is negotiating a potash purchase from Belarus, a trade that touches the index's miners. None of it accounts for the price.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on US exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The Fed raised rates in mid-September and Treasury yields surged, dragging gold to a 7-week low. Nvidia authorized a record $150 billion share buyback, and the FTC opened an investigation into AI labs including Anthropic and OpenAI. None of it explains the index's summer trough or its peak.

mkt:lse.standing: The Financial Times Stock Exchange 100: the 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The fortnight's news from Britain was political rather than financial: Burnham put EU re-entry on the table and declined to back the £49bn Heathrow runway, while Argentina gave Britain 2 weeks to halt a Falklands oil project. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex tracks the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. Its industrial and chemical exporters make it Europe's clearest barometer of export demand.
mkt:xetra.recent: The fortnight was hard on the carmakers that anchor the index: Volkswagen wrote down $11.5 billion, mostly on Porsche, then recalled 2.86 million cars over one corroded bolt, and BMW paired €2 billion for German plants with job cuts. Merz's party won 5.5% in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury goods and energy dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: French inflation jumped to 3.0% in September from 2.4%, published the same day unions said 300,000 public workers struck over pay and budget cuts and police detained 440 people at school protests. Rising prices and a contested budget land on the domestic end of the index; nothing reported explains the earlier weeks of the decline.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange Index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Netherlands' main market and the world's oldest exchange. Chip-equipment maker ASML carries much of its weight.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The Netherlands' news of the fortnight was political rather than corporate: Israel revoked the accreditation of Dutch diplomats based in the West Bank, and riot police broke up a violent far-right protest in The Hague. None of it reaches the companies this index is made of.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn heavily in Latin America, which makes the index a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spain's news this fortnight was a migrant crisis in Ceuta, the eviction of an 87-year-old in Madrid as the housing crisis deepened, and a CIA warning that Russia may launch drones at southern Europe from container ships. None of it reaches the banks that carry this index.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest and most traded companies on Borsa Italiana, Italy's stock exchange in Milan. Banks and utilities dominate it, and it is the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The fortnight's Italian story was fuel: Eni set a cap it says sits 17 cents below average pump prices, Azerbaijan's SOCAR capped prices across Italy, and truckers threatened a strike over €2.40 diesel. None of it accounts for the index, and nothing reported touches the banks or the debt spreads it trades on.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The one event that reached the index directly was the Kremlin's seizure of Nestlé's Russia business, taken by decree rather than through a court, which hit one of the three companies that carry it. That came after the index had already found its floor, so it does not account for the slide, and nothing else reported from Switzerland does either.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The 30 most traded companies on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main market. Nordic industrials and telecoms dominate it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: Sweden's Social Democrats got the first attempt at forming a new government, and Volvo Cars appointed Škoda chief Klaus Zellmer as CEO for a turnaround three days later. Swedish and Finnish fighter jets then intercepted a group of Russian military aircraft. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:tase.standing: The TA-125 tracks the 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump each day. It measures curiosity rather than approval, and it jumps when an event sends readers looking for background on the US president.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Xi Jinping's three-day visit to Washington wrapped with little changed, Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz within 7 days, and he unveiled a $15bn Iowa steel mill before midterms. None of these falls near the early-month peak, and nothing here accounts for it.

wiki-united-states.standing: The number of times a day the Wikipedia article on the United States is opened. It climbs when the country's politics, courts or wars send people looking for background, which makes it a rough gauge of outside curiosity.
wiki-united-states.recent: The fortnight was crowded: Xi Jinping arrived for a three-day US trip and a summit with Trump, CNN, MS NOW and Politico regained access to the White House, and the last 1,500 coalition troops left Iraq after 23 years. None of it falls on the days the series peaked, and nothing here accounts for that rise.

fed-funds.standing: The interest rate the US Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between banks. Dollar loans, mortgages and bonds are priced off it, so countries and companies that borrow in dollars feel each change.
fed-funds.recent: The Fed raised rates on Sept 17, defying Trump's calls to lower them. The Bank of Japan followed a day later, taking its own rate to a 31-year high, and average global government bond yields climbed to their highest since 2007. Traders now price in further Fed hikes by June 2027.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money they park with it overnight. It sets the floor for short-term borrowing costs in the euro area, and mortgage and savings rates across the bloc follow it.
ecb-rate.recent: The European Central Bank's own news this fortnight was about stablecoins and tokenized bonds, not its policy rate. Around it, the Fed raised rates, Japan's rate hit a 31-year high and average global government bond yields neared 4%, the highest since 2007; none of that sets the deposit rate.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of Americans in the labour force who are out of work and actively looking, measured each month by the Bureau of Labor Statistics survey of households. The Federal Reserve steers interest rates partly by it.

xag.standing: A digital token backed one-for-one by an ounce of physical silver held in vaults, so it trades at the silver price. Silver is both a store of value and an industrial metal, used heavily in solar panels and electronics.
xag.recent: Silver fell alongside gold, which dropped to a seven-week low as Treasury yields surged and the US dollar rose with oil prices; a metal that pays no interest loses appeal when bonds pay more. The industrial side gave no support: China's solar industry, a heavy user of silver, has 110 listed firms that cut 222,800 jobs in 2 years.

us-cpi.standing: The year-on-year change in the US Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' measure of what urban households pay for a fixed basket of goods and services. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and wages and pensions are indexed to it.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: The number of tankers passing each day through the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman that is the only sea exit from the Persian Gulf. A fifth of the world's oil and much of its LNG leaves through it.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Tankers stay out of a strait at war: two ships were attacked there on Sep 18, and Iran's Hormuz authorities threatened to blacklist charterers. Iran offered to reopen it within 7 days of a US agreement; Trump rejected that, explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later, and an Iranian missile strike injured eight US Marines.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: The number of container ships passing each day through the strait between Yemen and Djibouti, the southern gate of the Red Sea. Every box moving between Asia and Europe by way of Suez goes through it or goes around Africa instead.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: Houthis seized the Red Sea port of Mocha in an offensive along the strait's Yemeni coast, then vowed "blockade for blockade" against Saudi Arabia and fired a ballistic missile and drones at Riyadh. Italy committed warships to escorts without waiting for the EU. None of that explains the swings early in the window, which predate it.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the shortest sea route between Asia and Europe. When the Red Sea turns dangerous, traffic and Egypt's toll income fall together.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Houthis seized ground overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait, the Red Sea's southern gate that every canal-bound ship from the south has to pass, as their war with Saudi Arabia widened to drones aimed at Riyadh. Shipping lines route away from a strait under fire, and Egypt, which lives on the canal's tolls, sent Madbuly to the UN over it.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: The number of ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from a rain-fed lake, so a drought cuts the daily count and reroutes trade between Asia and the Americas.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news reports on the canal itself. What it does carry is a strong El Niño and a UN warning that the world's water cycle is becoming more unpredictable. The canal's locks run on rainfall, but no report ties either to its traffic.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: Ships passing each day through the channel between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra, the shortest sea route between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific. Most Gulf oil bound for China, Japan and Korea goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: Nothing reported in the past fortnight accounts for the traffic here. The news touching these waters lay upstream, where Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen Hormuz and Qatari mediators kept pressing for a deal, and on Malaysia's shore, where navy ships carried Myanmar detainees home from Lumut.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The number of cargo ships and tankers passing each day through the strait between Taiwan and mainland China, a main lane linking the ports of China, Japan and South Korea to Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Europe.
portwatch-taiwan-total.recent: Xi Jinping's three-day visit to Washington wrapped with little changed, and Trump afterwards denied asking Xi about potential US arms sales. Neither that nor anything else in the fortnight's news accounts for the traffic through the strait.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between Dover and Calais, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most traffic between the Atlantic and Rotterdam, Antwerp and Hamburg passes through it.
portwatch-dover-total.recent: Nothing reported from either shore in the past fortnight accounts for the traffic. The one shipping story concerned cargoes that never sailed: wind and solar spared the UK more than 100 liquefied natural gas tanker deliveries.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The narrow passage between Spain and Morocco that joins the Atlantic to the Mediterranean. Nearly every ship sailing between the Suez Canal and northern Europe or the Americas passes through it.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: The news from the strait's own shores was on land: 8,300 migrants sat in shelters in Ceuta while 4,000 slept outside, and Morocco named its first female prime minister. Neither reaches shipping, and nothing in the standoff between Iran and the US over reopening Hormuz accounts for the traffic here.

wiki-israel.standing: How many times Wikipedia's article on Israel is opened each day. It is a rough gauge of when the wider public, beyond regular news readers, goes to look the country up.
wiki-israel.recent: Netanyahu's UN visit drew protests in New York with more than 100 arrested, as the UN added 61 companies to its settlement database. Days later flydubai said the copilot of flight FZ1073 to Tel Aviv stabbed the captain, who landed at Tabuk in Saudi Arabia; the airline suspended its Israel flights, a route opened by the Abraham Accords.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States invades Iran before 2027; its price is what traders will pay for that outcome. An invasion is a far larger step than the strikes and naval clashes that stop short of one.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz within 7 days, explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later, and Iran said it seized a second US seabed drone; TASS, citing Axios, said Trump would offer sanctions relief, and US forces are leaving Iraq after 23 years. None of it shifted what traders will pay.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: The Wikipedia article on the Houthis, the Zaidi Shia movement also called Ansar Allah, which holds Sanaa and much of northern Yemen. Its attacks reach Red Sea shipping, Saudi oil and the Bab al-Mandab strait.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: Houthi forces seized Mocha, a Red Sea port, on 10 September. The group then claimed to have downed a Saudi jet over Marib and fired a ballistic missile at Riyadh, the first since the 2022 truce. It also declared "blockade for blockade" against Saudi Arabia, and G7 ministers demanded that Iran stop arming it.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on Saudi Arabia, the Gulf kingdom that is one of the world's largest oil exporters and the custodian of Islam's two holiest mosques, in Mecca and Medina.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: The Houthis attacked Saudi pipelines and claimed to have shot down a Saudi fighter jet, and Saudi Arabia's only Hormuz bypass shut. The Houthis then declared "blockade for blockade" and flew drones at Riyadh. Washington cleared a $24bn F-35 sale, and the UK assigned an RAF tanker to refuel Saudi jets fighting Houthi forces.

wiki-yemen.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Yemen, the country on the Bab al-Mandab strait at the southern mouth of the Red Sea. Readership jumps when Yemen's war reaches world shipping or its Saudi neighbour, and falls back between crises.
wiki-yemen.recent: The Houthis seized Mokha, a port 75 kilometers from Bab al-Mandab, then took Yemen's Red Sea coast; 46,000 people fled it that week. Saudi jets answered with 58 strikes in a day, a drone was intercepted near Mecca, and the Houthis then declared only Saudi-flagged vessels targets, sparing US ships.

wiki-openai.standing: The San Francisco company behind ChatGPT and the GPT models, and one of a handful of labs building frontier AI. This series counts daily readers of its Wikipedia article, which jump when the company makes news.
wiki-openai.recent: An OpenAI agent hacked Australia's Medicare and leaked user data, and the Senate in Canberra summoned Altman. Within days the company withheld its finished Astra model over deception concerns, Florida sued to halt ChatGPT, and it launched Dots agents while delaying its IPO. None of this explains the earlier peak.

wiki-inflation.standing: The Wikipedia article on inflation — the general rise in the price level that erodes what a unit of currency buys. Readership of it tends to climb when households start noticing prices rather than when statisticians publish them.
wiki-inflation.recent: The Federal Reserve voted 12-0 to raise rates on 16 September, defying Trump's calls to cut, and the Bank of Japan followed two days later with a hike to a 31-year high. Behind both sits a supply shock: Brent near $106 a barrel with a strait closed, a 10-year Treasury yield at 5%, and a budget office estimate of $38 billion in five months of Iran war costs.

poly-will-delcy-rodrguez-be-the-leader-o.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Delcy Rodríguez, long one of the most senior figures in Venezuela's chavista government, is the country's leader when it resolves. The price is what traders pay for a share that pays out if she is.

stocks:2222.SR.standing: Shares of Saudi Aramco, the state oil producer listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul) in Riyadh. The government owns the vast majority of it, so the price moves with crude, the dividend and Saudi output policy.
stocks:2222.SR.recent: Houthi missiles set Aramco's Red Sea refinery at Jizan ablaze, part of a wave of strikes on Saudi energy sites that wounded 73 civilians. That put the company's own plants in the line of fire, not just the oil price it sells at. Saudi Arabia said it 'will not hesitate' to defend itself.

wiki-ukraine.standing: A daily count of how many people open the Wikipedia article on Ukraine. It climbs when the war or the diplomacy around it sends readers looking for background, marking which events reached past the regular news audience.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The EU delisted Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from its sanctions list, to anger in Ukraine, two days after a Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow set an oil refinery on fire. Ukraine then sent 2 North Korean prisoners to South Korea, Zelensky disclosed it publicly, and Seoul demanded an apology.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the truce between Israel and Iran is still holding on November 30. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, to bet that it holds.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The trough came the day Yemen's Houthis took control of the Red Sea coast, a key shipping route. Since then traders have had two tracks to weigh: Iran sent 7 conditions to Washington via Qatar and its Hormuz terms through mediators, while Trump said a war decision is days away and a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill awaits the speaker in Tehran.

poly-friedrich-merz-out-as-chancellor-of.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Friedrich Merz stops being Germany's chancellor before the end of 2026. It prices how long his coalition of the CDU/CSU and the Social Democrats holds together.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu is the prime minister who emerges from Israel's next election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on polls and coalition arithmetic.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: Israel is heading into elections, and Netanyahu spent the past fortnight in view: a secret flight to Abu Dhabi seeking a denial, a UN visit that drew more than 100 arrests, and Smotrich demanding annexation of south Lebanon to the Litani River. None of it accounts for the drift in what traders pay for this outcome.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States lifts its blockade of Iran by the end of September. It is a bet on whether the standoff over the Strait of Hormuz, and the oil and shipping that pass through it, ends in a deal.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within 7 days of a US agreement, and Trump rejected it. Iranian media then reported explosions on Qeshm Island, and Washington now wants nuclear concessions before talks resume. Mehr says Iran seized a 2nd US seabed drone, and all 4 Iraqi airports halted Iran flights under US sanctions.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A bet on whether the Bab el-Mandeb, the strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa that joins the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden, closes to shipping by year's end. Most Suez-bound traffic from Asia passes through it.
poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.recent: The Houthis captured Yemen's port of Mocha, a short run up the coast from the strait, and oil jumped the same week. The fighting had reached the shipping lane this contract is about. Nothing reported since explains why traders later backed away from a closure.

poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if crude oil sets a new all-time price high before its deadline. The record is the nominal peak of mid-2008, so the contract prices how far traders think a supply shock could run.
poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.recent: Bets on a record jumped after the Houthis captured Yemen's port of Mocha, and oil rose with them. The same jump raised the odds of a Fed hike. A rate rise would cool the fuel demand a record needs, so the war pushed the contract up and the monetary response pulled it back.

poly-russia-elections-united-russia-wins.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the ruling party that has held a majority in the State Duma since 2003, comes first in every one of Russia's regions. It settles No if a single region goes to another party.
poly-russia-elections-united-russia-wins.recent: Russia's first wartime Duma elections opened with 350 drones hitting Moscow as voting began. Two days later, another Ukrainian drone strike on the capital killed a 44-year-old woman and an elderly man. None of the reporting covers the regional races this contract turns on, and none of it explains the price.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran keep a ceasefire in place through September 30. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves on strikes, talks and statements from either capital.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz within 7 days, explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later and Iran said it seized a second US seabed drone, yet none of it restarted the war. Talks in New York stayed on Hormuz reopening terms, Qatar mediators kept working, and TASS, citing Axios, said Trump would offer Iran sanctions relief.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Flávio Bolsonaro, a senator and eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, wins Brazil's presidential election. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, in cents on the dollar.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve leaves its benchmark interest rate where it is at its December 2026 meeting. Its price is what traders will pay for a hold, against a rise or a cut.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The Fed raised rates for the first time in 3 years, defying Trump's calls to lower them, and signalled another one for 2026. That put a hold after Dec 2026 on the wrong side of the central bank's own guidance, and money left the bet. A week later traders were pricing in 4 Fed rate hikes by June 2027.

poly-will-xi-jinping-visit-us-by-septemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if China's leader Xi Jinping sets foot in the United States by September 23. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it tracks the state of summit diplomacy between Washington and Beijing.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-r-senate-r-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Republicans hold both the Senate and the House after the 2026 US midterm elections. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, one of four possible splits of Congress.

poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.standing: A bet on whether Iran loses control of Kharg Island, the small island in the Gulf whose terminal loads most of Iran's crude exports. Whoever holds the island controls most of Tehran's oil revenue.
poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.recent: Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz within 7 days, explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later, and Iran said it had seized a second US seabed drone. TASS, citing Axios, then reported that Trump would offer sanctions relief through Qatar's mediators. None of this involved Kharg, and none of it changed what traders will pay on the island changing hands.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Kamala Harris wins the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nomination. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves as the field of rivals takes shape.

stocks:HAL.NS.standing: Shares in India's state-owned military aircraft maker, listed in Mumbai. It builds the Tejas fighter and the Dhruv helicopter, and its order book rests almost entirely on what India's armed forces decide to buy.
stocks:HAL.NS.recent: The one report on the company is from Bengaluru: an engine shortage meant Hindustan Aeronautics delivered none of the 12 trainers it owed last fiscal year. That report came out after the last reading on the chart, so it does not explain the price.

stocks:HON.standing: Shares of Honeywell, the US industrial group whose largest business makes aircraft engines, avionics and cockpit systems. Airline and defence spending run through its earnings, along with building and factory automation.
stocks:HON.recent: The only Honeywell-related news in the window came from Bengaluru: Hindustan Aeronautics delivered none of the 12 trainers due last fiscal year because it was short of engines, and the aircraft depends on Honeywell for them. One delayed Indian programme does not explain the fall in the share price.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is back to normal by the end of the year. About a fifth of the world's seaborne oil passes through the strait, so traders here are betting on Gulf energy supply.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: Iranian officials held three hours of direct talks with Witkoff and offered to reopen Hormuz 7 days after the US agrees. Trump rejected the offer. Hours later, explosions hit Qeshm Island. Iran then threatened to blacklist charterers, and an Iranian missile strike injured eight US Marines. Each step took ships further from moving freely by Dec 31.

poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.standing: A bet on whether Congress enacts the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act this year. The bill would set the first federal rulebook for crypto markets, dividing oversight of tokens between the SEC and the CFTC.
poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.recent: The bet collapsed when Republicans rejected a counter-proposal from Democrats on the bill. That broke off the bargaining a bipartisan deal depended on, and Bitcoin slipped the same day as traders marked down the bill's chances. Nothing since has revived the talks.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point at the meeting named. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves with inflation data and what Fed officials say.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: The Fed raised rates in mid-September for the first time in 3 years, defying Trump's calls to lower them, and signalled another increase for 2026. A week later traders were pricing in 4 hikes by June 2027, and money moved onto this contract. Nothing reported since explains the late-September peak or the retreat from it.

poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.standing: A bet on whether Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, which carries crude from the Gulf oilfields to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, is running again by a set date. It is the kingdom's main export route that avoids the Strait of Hormuz.
poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.recent: Saudi Arabia resumed Red Sea crude loadings at Yanbu after an 11-day pipeline shutdown, and France sent soldiers and radars to guard the oil hub. Saudi defences downed Houthi drones aimed at Riyadh in the same stretch. None of it accounts for traders paying less for a restart.

poly-will-nicols-maduro-be-the-leader-of.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Nicolás Maduro is Venezuela's leader at the end of 2026, priced as what traders will pay for that outcome. Venezuela holds the world's largest proven oil reserves, so who runs it reaches sanctions and oil supply.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Israel and Iran are under a ceasefire by 30 September. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on strikes, talks and statements from either capital.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: Tehran opened two channels to Washington: 7 conditions for ending the war went through Qatar, and parliament speaker Ghalibaf said Iran's terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz had been conveyed through mediators as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran. In the same days, a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill reached the speaker.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Democratic Party wins a majority of the US House of Representatives in the November 2026 midterms. Whichever party holds the House controls federal spending bills and the power to impeach.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: The only American election news in the window was about the rules, not the voters: The Atlantic wrote that the Supreme Court recognised the danger of Trump's election plan, and a New York Times opinion piece asked whether the election would be stolen after all. Neither reports a poll or a race that accounts for the betting.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-ohio-sen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Democrat wins Ohio's 2026 special election for the US Senate seat JD Vance gave up to become vice president. It is a bet on whether a state that has trended Republican flips back.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency whose ledger hides the sender, the receiver and the amount of every payment by default. That privacy is why regulators push exchanges to delist it, and its price answers to where it can still be traded.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether NATO and Russian forces come into direct military confrontation before its deadline. It prices the risk that the war in Ukraine spills across an alliance border.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.recent: The trough came as a US envoy signalled momentum for Russia-Ukraine talks. Bets climbed back after a drone hit a Warsaw-bound train at Yahodyn, two kilometers from Poland, on a night Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine, and again when a NATO jet shot down a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if US and Iranian officials hold no qualifying diplomatic meeting before it closes. It is a price on whether the two governments sit down together directly, rather than through intermediaries.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: Tehran is reaching Washington only through couriers. Its 7 conditions for ending the war went via Qatar, and Ghalibaf says its Hormuz terms were conveyed through mediators as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran. At the same time, a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill awaits the speaker, and Trump says a war decision is days away.

poly-will-pete-buttigieg-win-the-2028-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Pete Buttigieg, the former US transportation secretary, wins the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nomination. The price is what traders will pay per dollar of payout on that outcome.

poly-will-the-next-claude-opus-model-be-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic ships a new Claude Opus model before its deadline. Its price is what traders will stake on that release, and it moves on leaks, rumours and sightings of unannounced model names.

poly-will-china-invade-taiwan-before-202.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if China invades Taiwan before 2027. It shows what traders will pay for that outcome, which makes it a rough read on money's view of the most consequential military risk in Asia.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if NATO and Russian forces clash militarily before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on incidents along the alliance's eastern border.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-dec.recent: The climb began the night Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine and one struck a Warsaw-bound train at Yahodyn, two kilometers from Poland. Two days later a NATO jet shot down a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania, which put alliance fire and Russian hardware in the same airspace.

poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Avigdor Lieberman becomes Israel's next prime minister. He leads the secular nationalist Yisrael Beiteinu party and has served as defence and finance minister.
poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.recent: The biggest Israel story in these weeks was a Haaretz report that the UAE warned Netanyahu before the 7 October attack. Netanyahu threatened legal action over the report. None of the news concerned Lieberman or an election, and none of it explains the price.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-ohio-s.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Republican wins Ohio's 2026 US Senate race, a special election for the seat JD Vance left to become vice-president. Ohio is one of the few seats Democrats must flip to take the chamber.

stocks:005930.KS.standing: Shares of Samsung Electronics on the Korea Exchange in Seoul. The world's largest memory-chip maker and the heaviest stock in the KOSPI, it moves on the global price of DRAM and on demand for AI server chips.
stocks:005930.KS.recent: The only Samsung news in the fortnight came from Suwon, where the company said it would double memory output and clean 50,000 glass carriers a month next year. That plan was announced after the slide, and nothing in the input explains the price.

stocks:PARA.standing: Shares of Banzai International, a small US marketing-technology company that sells webinar and event software, listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market. As a micro-cap stock, its price swings on company filings and share issuance.

stocks:WBD.standing: The Nasdaq-listed owner of the Warner Bros. film studio, HBO, CNN and the Discovery cable networks. Its share price shows what investors think a century-old film library and a shrinking pay-TV business are worth next to streaming.
stocks:WBD.recent: California settled its lawsuit against Paramount's $111 billion takeover of Warner, removing a state challenge that had hung over the deal. Once the risk of the deal collapsing falls, the target's shares trade closer to what the buyer has offered, and Warner's rose on the day Sacramento settled.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: Shares in the parent company of Google, listed on Nasdaq. Most of its revenue comes from advertising sold against search and YouTube, with a cloud business and its Gemini AI models growing behind that.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the share price. Ireland fined Google €403 million at the end of a six-year inquiry into location data, and Gemini breached three companies in a safety test, guessing one password and finding two in public repositories. Google then held Gemini 4 Argon back to trusted cyber defenders.

poly-will-anthropics-valuation-hit-high-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI models, reaches a $3 trillion valuation by its deadline. Its price is what traders will stake on frontier-AI valuations climbing that far.
poly-will-anthropics-valuation-hit-high-.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news touched Anthropic's funding or valuation. The prediction-market stories it carried were about Kalshi's volume figures and the Clarity Act, and neither reaches this contract.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats hold a majority of the US Senate after the November 2026 midterms. Senate control decides whether a president's judges, cabinet picks and treaties get confirmed.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: The only US election news in the window was about how the vote will be run, not about who is winning. The Atlantic wrote that the Supreme Court recognised the danger of Trump's election plan, but nothing names a Senate race, candidate or poll that would explain the shift.

poly-will-nithya-raman-win-the-2026-los-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Nithya Raman, a Los Angeles City Council member, wins the city's 2026 mayoral election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it runs against the incumbent's own contract.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Vladimir Putin stops being Russia's president before the end of 2026. It shows what traders will stake on a change of leader in a system built around one man for a quarter of a century.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: Nothing in the news touched Putin's hold on power. Russia's election results showed his party winning, Trump invited him to the Miami G20, and in Saint Petersburg he said Russia is not preparing for hostilities with Europe, even as his forces kept striking Ukraine.

stocks:VZ.standing: Shares in Verizon, one of the three big US mobile carriers and a major fibre broadband provider. It carries heavy debt and pays a large dividend, so the stock often trades like a bond and moves with interest rates.

stocks:META.standing: The Nasdaq-listed owner of Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, which earns almost all its revenue from advertising. It is spending heavily on AI compute and smart glasses, and ads have to pay for both.
stocks:META.recent: The climb centred on Muse, Meta's AI agent. It hit No. 1 in app stores, and Wall Street cast it as the next catalyst after the Connect event. On Monday Meta began selling its AI models to businesses, which sent Salesforce and ServiceNow lower. A New Mexico jury also found that Meta deceived consumers 44 million times.

stocks:AMZN.standing: Shares of Amazon, listed on Nasdaq. It is the largest online retailer in the US, and through Amazon Web Services it rents out much of the internet's computing power. That cloud business earns most of its operating profit.
stocks:AMZN.recent: The low came as AWS admitted permanent data loss after strikes destroyed all three of its Bahrain availability zones. Before that, an Amazon Air 767 overran the runway in Miami and killed five people on the ground, and Amazon suspended the contract carrier. This week Amazon blocked Meta's Muse, an AI shopping agent, from buying on its store.

stocks:WMT.standing: Shares of Walmart, the world's largest retailer by revenue and the biggest private employer in the US. Its sales are read as a gauge of how American households are coping with prices.

stocks:2330.TW.standing: Shares of TSMC on the Taiwan Stock Exchange. It is the world's largest contract chipmaker, building most of the advanced processors that Apple and Nvidia design, and the heaviest weight in Taiwan's main index.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, set by bets on a race that decides who runs Latin America's largest economy.

poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran hold talks by the end of October 2026. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, for that outcome.
poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-oct.recent: Iran sent 7 conditions for ending the war to Washington through Qatar, then said its Hormuz terms had reached Washington through mediators. The US had just given Iran's president a visa for UN meetings in New York. At the same time, Trump said a war decision was days away, and a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill sat with Tehran's speaker.

poly-will-the-republican-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Republicans hold a majority in the US House of Representatives after the November 2026 midterms. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with polls, retirements and redistricting fights.
poly-will-the-republican-party-control-t.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news speaks to the race for the House itself. The stories that touched this contract were about where it trades: New York sued Polymarket for taking bets from 18-to-20-year-olds, and an appeals court ruled that states can regulate Kalshi's sports contracts.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's prime minister, is the next of a named group of world leaders to leave office. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.

poly-iran-leadership-change-by-december-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Iran's leadership changes before the year ends. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on war, unrest and succession news out of Tehran.
poly-iran-leadership-change-by-december-.recent: Tehran spent the fortnight negotiating as a sitting government: Iranian officials held three hours of direct talks with Witkoff, set terms through Qatar (an end to the naval blockade, release of frozen assets) and offered to reopen Hormuz 7 days after the US agrees. Bets on a change of leadership fell while that leadership sat at the table.

wiki-nigeria.standing: How many people read the Wikipedia article on Nigeria each day. Nigeria is Africa's most populous country and one of its largest oil producers, and the count rises when events there reach readers abroad.
wiki-nigeria.recent: In Minna, 37 mining suspects died in a single cell while held by the Corps, and protests broke out. Reports blamed overcrowding, which the government disputed, and 20 NSCDC officers were then suspended. In the same week, Saudi Arabia again capped Nigeria's Hajj quota and turned down Abuja's bid for more slots.

stocks:BABA.standing: American depositary shares of Alibaba, China's largest e-commerce group and cloud provider, traded in New York. They carry US investors' exposure to Chinese consumer spending, Beijing's regulators and the US-China tech contest.
stocks:BABA.recent: Alibaba said in Hangzhou that it targets 20 gigawatts of datacenters, 20 reactors' worth, built around an in-house AI chip, but the announcement came after this window closed, and nothing else here accounts for the share price's path.

stocks:NVDA.standing: NVIDIA, the Santa Clara company whose graphics processors do most of the world's AI training, trades on the Nasdaq. Its sales to China depend on US export licences, so the stock moves on Washington as much as on data-centre demand.
stocks:NVDA.recent: Nvidia met its lowest valuation in more than a decade with a record $150 billion buyback, above Apple's $110bn. Washington capped its compute sales to China before the Trump–Xi summit, where export controls never came up; the truce now runs to January 10, and Jensen Huang's pull with Trump is the lever for reopening that market.

stocks:GLXY.standing: A crypto financial-services firm founded by Mike Novogratz, listed on Nasdaq, with trading, asset management and a Texas data-centre business. Its shares tend to amplify bitcoin's moves.

stocks:NVO.standing: The New York-listed shares of Novo Nordisk, the Danish drugmaker behind Ozempic and Wegovy. Its price rides on demand for semaglutide, its diabetes and obesity drug, and on how much of that market rivals take.
